name: Edinburgh Napier University
description:
Edinburgh Napier University is located in the Scottish capital of Edinburgh.

Named after the 16th-century Scottish mathematician and philosopher John Napier, it has a strong history and reputation for teaching in the sciences and technology.

It has nearly 20,000 students from over 140 nations internationally. It has been awarded the Queen's Anniversary Prize twice, most recently in 2015 for its work in timber engineering, sustainable construction and wood science.

What is the Edinburgh Napier University acceptance rate for International Students?

The Edinburgh Napier University acceptance rate is 56%.

Edinburgh Napier University offers a diverse range of facilities to support its students. The Merchiston campus is where students can find advanced computing facilities and media studios, while the Sighthill campus is famed for its health and social sciences resources. Edinburgh Napier University places a robust emphasis on technology that is reflected in its IT services and dedicated computing spaces. The sports facilities provided at Engage include fitness classes, a fully-equipped gym and sports halls for hire.

Student Life

The university has three campuses: Craiglockhart Campus, overlooking Edinburgh, which is home to the Business School, Merchiston campus, where computing and creative students are likely to be based, and Sighthill campus, where over 5,000 students are based. The School of Applied Sciences and the School of Health & Social Care are located here.

highlights.title: Overview
highlights.value:
Edinburgh Napier University (ENU) is a leading modern university in Scotland, originally founded in 1964 as Napier Technical College. It was named after the famous 16th-century mathematician John Napier and gained full university status in 1992. Today, you’ll find a community of nearly 20,000 students from over 145 countries.

The university is spread across five specialist schools: Applied Sciences, Arts & Creative Industries, Business, Computing, Engineering & the Built Environment, and Health & Social Care. ENU is particularly well-regarded for its industry-focused teaching and has twice been awarded the Queen’s Anniversary Prize for its innovative work in timber engineering and sustainable construction.

highlights.title: Student life
highlights.value:
When you join ENU, you’ll become part of an international, collaborative community based in the heart of Scotland's capital. You can get involved with the Edinburgh Napier Students’ Association (ENSA), which supports numerous societies and sports clubs, from academic groups to recreational activities.

Living in Edinburgh means you are never far from culture. From the historic Old Town to the lively festivals that take place year-round, there is always something for you to explore. The university also provides comprehensive support services to help you settle into life in the UK.

highlights.title: Accommodation
highlights.value:
You can choose from a range of modern, purpose-built student accommodation sites located in and around the city centre.

Flats typically house between four and eight people and come equipped with smart TVs in communal lounges, full kitchen facilities, and bedrooms with study desks. For your peace of mind, the university provides 24-hour security and CCTV across all its sites.

If you’re looking for budget-friendly accommodation options outside the campus, feel free to download our app and check out the Stays feature!

highlights.title: Facilities
highlights.value:
1. Library

You’ll have access to extensive learning resource centres across the campuses, including the 24-hour Jack Kilby Computing Centre at Merchiston, which offers 500 computers for student use.

2. Sports

You can stay active at the [EN]GAGE sports centre located at the Sighthill campus. It features a gym, fitness classes, and sports halls for various team activities.

3. Laboratories

ENU offers industry-standard facilities, including clinical skills laboratories, specialised biomechanics labs, hospital wards for nursing students, and high-tech cybersecurity labs.

4. Cafeteria

You can grab a meal at one of the main on-campus restaurants: the Hydra at Craiglockhart, the Atrium at Sighthill, or the Triangle at Merchiston. There are also Edinburgh Espresso Labs for quick coffee breaks.
